Bounds of a group sequential design

Source: R/gs_bounds.R
gs_bounds.Rd

Computes one-sided efficacy bounds by alpha spending and, optionally, futility bounds that are fixed or obtained by beta spending, for a vector of standardized statistics with a multivariate normal distribution.

Usage

gs_bounds(
  info_frac,
  alpha = 0.025,
  sf_eff = "OF",
  param_eff = NULL,
  futility = c("none", "fixed", "beta"),
  fut_bound = NULL,
  sf_fut = "OF",
  param_fut = NULL,
  beta = 0.1,
  binding = FALSE,
  mean = NULL,
  corr = NULL,
  sigma_alt = NULL
)

Arguments

info_frac

Information fractions used for spending (strictly increasing and ending at 1).

alpha

One-sided type I error.

sf_eff, param_eff

Alpha spending function and its parameter (see gs_spend).

futility

"none", "fixed" or "beta".

fut_bound

Fixed futility bounds on the Z scale at looks 1 to K - 1 (for futility = "fixed").

sf_fut, param_fut

Beta spending function and its parameter.

beta

Total type II error for beta spending.

binding

Whether the futility bounds are binding.

mean

Mean vector of the statistics under the alternative (required for futility = "beta").

corr

Correlation matrix of the statistics under the null hypothesis. Defaults to sqrt(t_j / t_k) for j <= k with t = info_frac.

sigma_alt

Covariance matrix of the statistics under the alternative. Defaults to corr.

Value

A data frame with one row per look: look, info_frac, cumulative alpha_spent and beta_spent, the efficacy bound upper, the futility bound lower (-Inf when there is none) and the one-sided nominal p-value of the efficacy bound nominal_p.

Details

The efficacy bound at look k solves, under the null hypothesis (mean 0, correlation corr), the equation that the probability of continuing to look k and then crossing the bound equals the alpha spent at look k. With binding = TRUE the continuation region at the earlier looks includes the futility bounds; with binding = FALSE the futility bounds are ignored for the efficacy bounds.

With futility = "beta", the futility bound at look k solves, under the alternative (mean mean, covariance sigma_alt), the equation that the probability of continuing to look k and then falling below the bound equals the beta spent at look k. The mean may take any value at each look, so that non-proportional hazards are allowed. A futility bound above the efficacy bound is set to the efficacy bound. At the last look the futility bound equals the efficacy bound.

All probabilities are computed with mvtnorm::pmvnorm() and the Miwa algorithm.

References

Lan KKG, DeMets DL (1983). Discrete sequential boundaries for clinical trials. Biometrika 70:659-663.

See also

gs_spend, gs_prob, ms_power

Examples

# O'Brien-Fleming type efficacy bounds at 50, 75 and 100 percent
gs_bounds(c(0.5, 0.75, 1))
#>   look info_frac alpha_spent beta_spent    upper    lower   nominal_p
#> 1    1      0.50 0.001525323         NA 2.962588     -Inf 0.001525323
#> 2    2      0.75 0.009649325         NA 2.359018     -Inf 0.009161689
#> 3    3      1.00 0.025000000         NA 2.014084 2.014084 0.022000375

# Non-binding futility by beta spending with a delayed effect
gs_bounds(c(0.5, 0.75, 1), futility = "beta", sf_fut = "HSD",
          param_fut = -2, mean = c(0.8, 1.9, 2.8))
#>   look info_frac alpha_spent beta_spent    upper      lower   nominal_p
#> 1    1      0.50 0.001525323 0.02689414 2.962588 -1.1285377 0.001525323
#> 2    2      0.75 0.009649325 0.05449458 2.359018  0.1920799 0.009161689
#> 3    3      1.00 0.025000000 0.10000000 2.014084  2.0140837 0.022000375
